reason: Entrypoint registers five implemented GA4 Data API report tools and one local configured-property echo. The property-listing description overstates its implementation; no Admin API client or listing exists.

tools.name: ga4_run_report
tools.description: Run an arbitrary GA4 runReport query. Most flexible tool — use when the convenience tools below do not cover what you need.

propertyId.description: GA4 property ID. Falls back to GA4_PROPERTY_ID env if not provided.

dateRanges.description: Date ranges. Each item is {startDate, endDate} with "YYYY-MM-DD" or relative "NdaysAgo" / "today" / "yesterday".

orderBy.description: Metric name to sort desc by. Optional.

tools.behavior: Calls runReport on the selected property, maps metric/dimension name arrays to name objects, forwards dateRanges unchanged, optionally sorts a single metric descending, and uses args.limit || 100. Formats response rows using dimension and metric headers and returns property, the number of returned rows, and rows as JSON text.
notes: The exposed request is a restricted runReport subset: no filters, pagination offset, metric aggregations, or cohortSpec are exposed. Date range objects are forwarded unchanged, including any additional fields allowed by the schema. limit uses a truthiness fallback, so zero becomes 100; no numeric constraints are registered.

tools.name: ga4_realtime
tools.description: Active users right now + top countries + events in the last 30 minutes.
tools.behavior: Calls runRealtimeReport with activeUsers and country/deviceCategory dimensions. Returns property and formatted realtime rows as JSON text.
notes: Description promises events and top countries, but the handler requests only activeUsers grouped by country and deviceCategory, with no event metric/dimension or ranking.

tools.name: ga4_top_events
tools.description: Top events by count over last N days.
tools.behavior: Calls runReport with eventCount by eventName over Number(args.days) || 7 daysAgo through today, descending eventCount sort, and Number(args.limit) || 20 rows. Returns property, days, and topEvents as JSON text.
notes: days and limit are converted with Number and truthiness defaults: zero falls back; no positive/integer constraints are registered.

tools.name: ga4_daily_users
tools.description: Daily active users and sessions over last N days.
tools.behavior: Calls runReport with activeUsers, sessions, and newUsers by date over Number(args.days) || 28 daysAgo through today, ascending date order, and days + 10 row limit. Returns property, days, and daily rows as JSON text.
notes: Also returns newUsers, beyond the description. days is converted with Number and truthiness default, so zero falls back; no positive/integer constraints are registered.

tools.name: ga4_retention
tools.description: Retention-style cohort view: active users by firstSessionDate (cohort) and date (day of return).

days.description: How many days back to look. Default 28.

tools.behavior: Calls runReport with activeUsers by firstSessionDate and date over Number(args.days) || 28 daysAgo through today and Number(args.limit) || 500 row limit. Returns property, days, and retention rows as JSON text.
notes: This is a dimension-based report, not an Analytics Data API cohortSpec request or calculated retention rate. days and limit use Number and truthiness defaults; no positive/integer constraints are registered.

tools.name: ga4_list_properties
tools.description: List GA4 properties accessible to the service account. Useful if the Property ID is unclear.
tools.behavior: Returns local JSON text containing DEFAULT_PROPERTY and a note suggesting the Admin API and asserting access to the default property. Makes no API request, does not enumerate accessible properties, and does not verify access.
notes: Misleading advertised description: this is a configured-ID echo, not an Admin API property listing. The claimed service-account access is unverified. Its empty input schema exposes no propertyId, yet the common dispatcher resolves a property before reaching this branch; without GA4_PROPERTY_ID (or an unadvertised propertyId argument), it throws before the try/catch.
Source review only; no tools/list, upstream execution, or live requests performed. Git HEAD matches the supplied revision.

All six tools are unconditionally listed after successful credential initialization; no optional modules or permission tiers. Startup exits before registration when none of GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, GA4_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON, or GA4_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64 is set, or when inline credentials cannot be parsed. package.json points main/bin/start to server.js and requires Node >=18.

Every call resolves args.propertyId or GA4_PROPERTY_ID before the handler try/catch. Missing/blank property throws outside the formatted GA4 error response. Non-prefixed IDs are prefixed with properties/.
Registered schemas omit additionalProperties, required lists except on ga4_run_report and its dateRanges items, and numeric bounds. Defaults mentioned in descriptions are not schema default keywords.

review.method: Root compared every explicit schema, description and dispatcher, confirmed configured-ID echo and corrected promised realtime events; preserved schema omission of handler-only defaults.
